findings.claim: claude.okf-mcp has nothing to check. The Claude install does not declare okf's MCP server anywhere: in spike:apm-only-install/1 APM warned "Transitive package 'okf' declares self-defined MCP server 'bundle'" and wrote no .mcp.json (the other files were apm-hooks.json, the okf stop hook, settings.json, .gitignore, the lock and apm.yml), and apm-only-install's plan never writes one. So either the check always fails, which breaks Done-when (exit 0 with every check ok) and r1, or it checks nothing. The plan must drop claude.okf-mcp, or say which ticket makes the Claude install declare the server (that changes apm-only-install's contract).

The sha256 check of every lock-listed deployed file may fail on every correct install. APM writes okf's hook into .claude/settings.json (spike:apm-only-install/1: '1 hook(s) integrated -> .claude/settings.json'; for Antigravity it writes .agents/hooks.json), and kmctl then merges its own SessionStart entry into that same settings.json. If apm.lock.yaml lists settings.json (or apm-hooks.json, .agents/hooks.json) in deployed_file_hashes, kmctl's merge changes the hash and doctor reports a broken install that is fine. No spike shows a lock from a hook-bearing install. Spike question: after an APM 0.33.0 install with the pinned okf-skills dependency for claude and antigravity, followed by merging a SessionStart entry into .claude/settings.json, does deployed_file_hashes list any hook or settings file, and does every listed hash still match the bytes on disk?

The read-only, no-network contract rests on two real commands nobody has run that way: `uv tool run --offline --from apm-cli==0.33.0 apm --version` (uv may build or link a tool env in its cache under HOME; APM may check for a newer version) and `claude plugin list --json` (the claude CLI writes ~/.claude.json on start and may refresh marketplaces). r5 checks HOME and sockets but the unit tests use fake tools, so it would pass while the real doctor writes and connects. Spike question: with a scratch HOME and XDG cache whose uv cache already holds apm-cli 0.33.0, and with networking blocked (unshare -n or strace -f -e trace=connect), do those two commands open a connection or change any file under HOME? If they do, the plan has to change how doctor checks APM and the old plugin, or narrow its promise.

User scope is out of the plan, but apm-only-install keeps `kmctl plugin install --scope user` (apm install -g, state and lock in ~/.apm/, files and hook under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR). Doctor only reads the repository, so after a user-scope install it prints `no kmctl harness in this repository; run kmctl plugin install --harness claude` and exits 1: a false failure with a fix that installs a second copy at project scope. Since doctor replaces `plugin status`, the plan must say whether doctor checks the user-scope install (~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml, $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json) or names it as found elsewhere rather than failing.

antigravity.plugin checks that `.agents/plugins/kmctl/` 'holds its 4 files', but antigravity-harness writes plugin.json, hooks.json, mcp_config.json and three agents (kmctl-auditor plus okf's bundle-weaver and event-analyzer), 6 files unless okf's agents are cut. Its `plugin status --harness antigravity` also compares each file with what this CLI would write and reports missing, extra or different files. Doctor removes `plugin status` but keeps only a presence count, so a hand-edited hooks.json or a stale translated agent goes unreported. The plan should reuse antigravity-harness's comparison function rather than a count. It should also say what happens when apm_modules/ (gitignored, the source of okf's agents) is absent, as in a fresh clone.
claude.okf-mcp now checks the okf-bundle entry apm-only-install merges into .mcp.json (or the user-scope entry), built by the same function, so there is something to check.
spike:kmctl-doctor/3 shows the lock never lists .claude/settings.json, .agents/hooks.json or apm-hooks.json, and all 32 listed hashes matched after a kmctl-style merge.

spike:kmctl-doctor/4 shows claude plugin list connects and writes, so the plan drops it and reads enabledPlugins from the settings file; the offline uv tool run made no connection and changed nothing under HOME.
The plan adds kmctl doctor --scope user and a claude.scope ok line when only a user-scope install exists; eval row r3b covers both.

antigravity.plugin now compares every file under .agents/plugins/kmctl/ with what the CLI would write, reusing antigravity-harness's comparison, and a missing apm_modules/ fails with a named fix; r2 covers it.

claude.old-plugin tells the user to run kmctl plugin install --harness claude for okf@scaccogatto too, but install cannot remove that plugin in the common cases. remove_old_plugin (src/kmctl/plugin.py:282) acts only when claude plugin list shows kmctl@kmctl for this folder, then runs prune, which keeps an okf the user installed on purpose. A repository whose settings still enable okf@scaccogatto without kmctl@kmctl (kmctl removed by hand, or okf installed on its own) therefore fails doctor for good, and the fix it prints does nothing.

The --online check adds httpx as a runtime dependency, which locks in six new packages (httpx, httpcore, h11, anyio, certifi, idna), for one optional HEAD request. The standard library's urllib.request would do the same job. Tests could then patch the fetch, and respx would not be needed either.

entries.change: claude.old-plugin names `kmctl plugin install --harness claude` only when kmctl@kmctl is enabled; an okf@scaccogatto enabled on its own gets `claude plugin uninstall okf@scaccogatto --scope project|local|user`, from the settings file it was found in. Only kmctl@kmctl, not okf alone, marks the claude harness as installed.

test_old_plugin_enabled_fails_with_its_fix covers kmctl@kmctl, both together, and okf alone in settings.json and settings.local.json with each fix line; test_old_okf_plugin_alone_does_not_mark_the_claude_harness; the user-scope okf case expects the uninstall fix at user scope.
The claude.old-plugin row gives both fixes.
Kept httpx. The repository rule .claude/rules/httpx-for-http.md requires HTTP calls through httpx, not urllib.request, so switching would break a project rule; respx stays as its test double.

findings.claim: claude.old-plugin gave the install fix for an okf@scaccogatto enabled on its own, which the install never removes
httpx is a new runtime dependency for one HEAD request
